claim: AWS Data Exchange is a service that helps AWS customers easily share and manage data entitlements from other organizations at scale.
question: What is AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: share and manage data entitlements from other organizations at scale
AWS Data Exchange is a service

evidence.quote: AWS Data Exchange is a service that helps AWS customers easily share and manage data entitlements from other organizations at scale.

claim: As a data receiver you can track and manage all your data grants and AWS Marketplace data subscriptions in one place, and use compatible AWS or partner analytics and machine learning services on the data.
question: What can a data receiver do in AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: track and manage all of your data grants and AWS Marketplace data subscriptions in one place
compatible AWS or partner analytics and machine learning

evidence.quote: As a data receiver, you can track and manage all of your data grants and AWS Marketplace data subscriptions in one place. When you have access to an AWS Data Exchange data set, you can use compatible AWS or partner analytics and machine learning to extract insights from it.

claim: For data senders, AWS Data Exchange eliminates the need to build and maintain data delivery and entitlement infrastructure, and anyone with an AWS account can create and send data grants.
question: Why would a data provider use AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: eliminates the need to build and maintain any data delivery and entitlement infrastructure
Anyone with an AWS account can create and send data grants

evidence.quote: For data senders, AWS Data Exchange eliminates the need to build and maintain any data delivery and entitlement infrastructure. Anyone with an AWS account can create and send data grants to data receivers.

claim: Anyone, with or without an AWS account, can find and use publicly available data sets that are part of the Open Data on AWS program.
question: Do you need an AWS account to use Open Data on AWS data sets?

values.display: anyone, with or without an AWS account
publicly available data sets

evidence.quote: In addition, anyone, with or without an AWS account, can find and use publicly available data sets that are part of the [Open Data on AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/opendata/) program.
Anyone can search and find these free Open Data on AWS data sets, with or without an AWS account, no subscription required.

claim: A data grant is the unit of exchange created by a data sender to give a data receiver access to a data set; the receiver accepts the grant to gain access to the underlying data.
question: What is a data grant in AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: the unit of exchange in AWS Data Exchange
A data receiver accepts the data grant to gain access to the underlying data

evidence.quote: A data grant is the unit of exchange in AWS Data Exchange that is created by a data sender in order to grant a data receiver access to a data set. When a data sender creates a data grant, a grant request is sent to the data receiver's AWS account. A data receiver accepts the data grant to gain access to the underlying data.

claim: AWS Data Exchange supports five types of data sets: Files, API, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, and AWS Lake Formation (Preview).
question: Which data set types does AWS Data Exchange support?

values.display: supports five types of data sets
Files, API, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, and AWS Lake Formation (Preview)

evidence.quote: AWS Data Exchange supports five types of data sets: Files, API, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, and AWS Lake Formation (Preview).

claim: A product is the unit of exchange in AWS Marketplace, published by a provider for subscribers, and a data product is a product that includes AWS Data Exchange data sets; it is listed after AWS reviews it against guidelines and terms.
question: What is an AWS Marketplace data product?

values.display: A data product is a product that includes AWS Data Exchange data sets
reviewed by AWS against our guidelines and terms and conditions

evidence.quote: A product is the unit of exchange in AWS Marketplace that is published by a provider and made available for use to subscribers. A data product is a product that includes AWS Data Exchange data sets. When a data provider publishes a data product, that product is listed in the AWS Marketplace product catalog after being reviewed by AWS against our guidelines and terms and conditions.

claim: With Files data sets, subscribers can access a copy of the data set as an entitled data set and export the assets.
question: What does a subscriber get from a Files data set?

values.display: access a copy of the data set as an entitled data set
export the assets

evidence.quote: Using Files, subscribers can access a copy of the data set as an entitled data set and export the assets.

claim: With Amazon Redshift datashare assets, recipients get read-only access to query the data in Amazon Redshift without extracting, transforming and loading data.
question: Can a subscriber query shared Redshift data without ETL?

values.display: read-only access to query the data in Amazon Redshift
without extracting, transforming, and loading data

evidence.quote: With Amazon Redshift datashare assets, recipients can get read-only access to query the data in Amazon Redshift without extracting, transforming, and loading data.

claim: With Amazon S3 data access assets, subscribers directly access and use the provider's data without creating or managing data copies, and providers can share an entire S3 bucket, specific prefixes or objects.
question: How can a provider share S3 data without copying it?

values.display: directly access and use the provider's data without creating or managing data copies
share direct access to an entire S3 bucket or specific prefixes

evidence.quote: With Amazon S3 data access assets, recipients or subscribers can directly access and use the provider's data without creating or managing data copies. Data set owners can set up AWS Data Exchange for Amazon S3 on top of their existing Amazon S3 buckets to share direct access to an entire S3 bucket or specific prefixes and Amazon S3 objects.

claim: With API assets, subscribers can make API calls to AWS Data Exchange-managed endpoints, which are proxied through to the API owner's endpoints, and the data set owner adds an existing Amazon API Gateway API.
question: How do subscribers call an API shared through AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: make API calls to AWS Data Exchange-managed endpoints
proxied through to API-owner endpoints

evidence.quote: You can also make API calls to AWS Data Exchange-managed endpoints, which are then proxied through to API-owner endpoints.

claim: To be finalized, a revision must contain at least one asset, and a finalized revision published to at least one data grant or product cannot be unfinalized or changed except through the revoke revision process.
question: Can you change a finalized AWS Data Exchange revision?

values.display: a revision must contain at least one asset
can't be unfinalized or changed in any way

evidence.quote: To be finalized, a revision must contain at least one asset.
A finalized revision published to at least one data grant or product can't be unfinalized or changed in any way. (Except through the revoke revision process)

evidence.quote: AWS Data Exchange jobs are asynchronous import or export operations.

claim: The Open Data on AWS program is a collection of over 300 free, publicly available data sets, and unless stated otherwise data sets in the Registry of Open Data on AWS are provided and maintained by third parties under a variety of licenses, not by AWS.
question: Who maintains Open Data on AWS data sets?

values.display: over 300 free, publicly available data sets
are not provided and maintained by AWS

evidence.quote: The [Open Data on AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/opendata/) program is a collection of over 300 free, publicly available data sets.
Unless specifically stated in the applicable data set documentation, data sets that are available through the Registry of Open Data on AWS are not provided and maintained by AWS.
